subject: giant Pacific octopus
title: Sharks Kept Vanishing From an Aquarium Tank. The Killer Had No Bones

scenes.text: Sharks kept dying in one aquarium tank. Nobody saw who did it.
The tank held spiny dogfish, small sharks with venomous spines.
It also held a giant Pacific octopus, the biggest octopus species on Earth.
Then the aquarium's camera caught it in the act.
The octopus wrapped its arms around a shark and held on.
The killer was the soft, boneless animal everyone assumed was the shark's lunch.

description:
Spiny dogfish sharks kept dying in an aquarium tank, until a camera caught the culprit: the giant Pacific octopus sharing the tank.
The footage shows the octopus wrapping a shark in its arms. Giant Pacific octopuses are the largest octopus species, with up to 280 suckers on each arm.
Who would you have bet on, shark or octopus?
first_comment: Each arm of a giant Pacific octopus carries up to 280 suckers. Octopus or shark: who wins in open water?
